finding.claim: GET /users returns id and name of every user in any org the caller names, with no authentication and no check that the caller belongs to that org.
finding.sink: req.pg.query(...) at db.js:9 returns the user directory for that org; res.json(rows) at db.js:10.

trace.note: Route registered with no auth middleware or session check.
org taken directly from query string and used as the filter; not compared to caller identity or org.
All matching rows returned; no limit or pagination.

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query ($1) so no SQL injection; no auth middleware on this route in this file; no binding of org to caller tenant/session; no response field filtering. Confidence medium: global middleware outside this file is not visible.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers GET /users with no auth middleware. db.js:9 takes req.query.org directly as the query parameter with no comparison to caller identity or session. db.js:10 returns all rows with no limit. The parameterized query ($1) at db.js:9 prevents SQL injection but is not an authorization control. The app has no app.use() anywhere in db.js (lines 5-23), and no other source files exist in the directory.
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 exposes id and name for every user in any org named in req.query.org with no authentication or org-membership check, so an anonymous attacker can enumerate any tenant's user directory. The only caveat is that req.pg (db.js:9) is not defined in this directory, so a global auth middleware could exist outside the provided code; nothing visible in the codebase guards this route.

finding.claim: If no middleware sets req.pg, a single unauthenticated GET /users request can crash the process.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated HTTP request to GET /users.
finding.sink: req.pg.query at db.js:9 throws TypeError inside async handler; unhandled rejection.

trace.note: req.pg is never assigned in this file; access throws if undefined.
Express 4 does not catch async handler rejections; request gets no response and on Node 15+ the process terminates.

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch or .catch() around handler; no process-level unhandledRejection handler in this file. Confidence low: depends on unseen deployment setup.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers the handler with no try/catch or .catch(). Nothing in the directory sets req.pg: db.js is the only file, and it has no app.use or middleware. The file has no process.on('unhandledRejection') handler. No guard sits between the anonymous request and the throw.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: db.js:9 reads req.pg.query with req.pg never assigned, so an anonymous GET /users (db.js:8) throws a TypeError inside an async handler that Express 4 does not catch, leaving an unhandled rejection that crashes Node 15+ by default. The one residual uncertainty is a deployment that injects req.pg from outside this directory, which the available code cannot rule out, so the finding holds on the code as given.
